name: Likuba
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Adoua, Jean-Marie. 1981. Description phonologique du likuba (langue bantu du Congo). Thesis; also Ndinga Oba 2003 (C20 typological study). Neither found online.

sources.citation: Fontaney, Louise. 1988. Mboshi: Steps toward a Grammar: Part I. Pholia 3: 87-168 (Lab. de Phonétique et Linguistique Africaine, Lyon 2).
sources.note: Describes Mboshi (C25), not Likuba; Likuba (likùbà) is only named on p. 88 as a language 'spoken around Mossaka' mutually intelligible with Likwala and not understood by Mboshi speakers. No Likuba stress or tone statement.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page and JSON for liku1242 (MED list: Mowel 2012, Ndinga Oba 2003, Adoua 1981, Lebeuf 1962/64) and BibTeX of refs 21050, 581218, 101227, 41356, 118707.
sources.note: Bibliographic only. Confirms the descriptive universe: Adoua 1981 (130-pp. phonology mémoire, Brazzaville), Ndinga Oba 2003 (C20 typology, 'Likuba of Bohoulou', 33 pp. on Likuba), Mowel 2012 (negation), Ndamba 1987 (atlas), Lebeuf 1962/64 (myth).

sources.citation: Motingea Mangulu, André & Balthazar Biako Montanga Mayika. 2015. Notes sur les parlers Mɔ́yɛ́ du Moyen Congo (bantou C38). Journal of Asian and African Studies (ILCAA) 92: 5-122.
sources.note: About Moye (C38); names Likuba (C27) only as western neighbour (p. 7) and in its literature survey (p. 12: phonological sketch of Likuba = Adoua 1981; typological study of the whole C20 group = Ndinga Oba 2004a/b). No Likuba stress statement.

sources.citation: 'Likuba Genesis Translation' (BFBS 1916), Rosetta Project item tagged kxx on archive.org.
sources.note: Not C27 Likuba at all: the text ('Mukanda a Buxi a Mosese... Ncembi') is Bushong/Kuba of Kasai (DRC); the Rosetta Project mis-tagged it. No description, no stress information.

sources.citation: Wikipedia 'Kuba language' (kxx, C.27) and 'Bangi language' (raw wikitext).
sources.note: No phonology; 'Kuba language' cites only Ethnologue, Maho 2009 and Nurse & Philippson 2003. 'Bangi language' says Likuba people used Bobangi as a trade language in the 1890s (Meeuwis 2019, 2023).
